# JLang

> JLang is a small, open, bytecode-interpreted language for programming microcontrollers and learning how hardware works. 32-bit wrapping ints, first-class bit slicing, manual but checked memory, a desktop board simulator with virtual time, and interrupt-style event handlers. Implemented in portable C99.

## Tooling
- `jlang check FILE` compile only. Exit 0 = ok, 65 = compile error. Errors: `error (line L, col C): message` + source line + caret.
- `jlang run FILE [--emit EVENT]... [--pin N=0|1] [--analog N=0..4095] [--distance CM] [--answer TEXT] [--voice TEXT] [--kv K=V] [--heap BYTES] [--max-cycles N] [--stats]` run on the simulated board. Exit 70 = runtime error: `runtime error (line L): message` + call trace. Unfreed memory is reported at exit as `leak: ...` on stderr.
- `jlang test FILE...` run built-in `test "name" { ... }` blocks. Each test runs in an isolated VM with a fresh heap and virtual clock reset to 0 ms; assertion failures or memory leaks fail the test.
- `jlang fmt FILE... [-w|--write] [--check]` zero-config source formatter (pass `-` for stdin; `--check` exits 1 if formatting differs).
- `jlang bundle FILE [-o OUT]` resolves all `use` and `use ... as alias` imports into one standalone `.jlang` file for the browser WASM playground and ESP32 VM firmware.
- More `run` options: `--temperature C` (simulated I2C sensor), `--for SECONDS` (how long timers run, default 10), `--vcd FILE` (every pin as a VCD waveform for GTKWave), `--panel WxH`, `--realtime`.
- `jlang xray FILE` trace every instruction. `jlang dis FILE` print bytecode. `jlang new NAME` scaffold a project.
- `jlang wcet FILE [--mhz N]` worst-case cycles of the script and each `on` handler from the machine code (only `for i in A..B` with constant bounds is bounded). `jlang svd CHIP.svd [--only GPIO,UART0.FIFO] [-o FILE]` prints registers as consts: NAME (address), NAME_HI/NAME_LO (bit field), NAME_BIT (one bit).
- Editor & AI tooling: `editors/vscode/server.mjs` (zero-dependency stdio LSP for diagnostics, hover, completion, formatting) and `tools/jlang-mcp/index.mjs` (zero-dependency MCP server exposing `jlang_check`, `jlang_run`, `jlang_test`, `jlang_wcet`, `jlang_emu`, `jlang_fmt`).

## Syntax
- No semicolons. Blocks `{ }`. Conditions without parentheses. Comments `//` and `/* */`.
- `use "relative/file.jlang"` or `use "relative/file.jlang" as alias` top level only: include-once module import (diamond-safe, cycle-checked, per-file error diagnostics). With `as alias`, declarations (`const`, `enum`, `struct`, `let`, `fn`) live in that module's namespace and are accessed as `alias.NAME` / `alias.Enum.MEMBER` so independent drivers never collide. Works in VM and native RISC-V; run `jlang bundle` to deploy multi-file projects to browser WASM or ESP32 firmware.
- `let x = 1` (top level = global, in a block = local). `let y` is nil.
- `fn name(a, b) { return a + b }` top level only. Functions are values.
- `if c { } else if d { } else { }`, `match x { 0 => { } 1, 2 => { } _ => { } }`, `while c { }`, `for i in 0..n { }` (end exclusive), `break`, `continue`. When matching on an `enum` value without `_`, every enum member must be handled (compile error lists missing members) and duplicate enum arms are rejected.
- `defer stmt` or `defer { ... }`: runs in reverse (LIFO) order when the enclosing scope exits (normal end, `return`, `break`, `continue`). Return expressions evaluate before defers. Works in VM and native code.
- `on EVENT { }` top level only; runs when the host fires EVENT (`--emit EVENT` or `emit("EVENT")`). On ESP32, BOOT fires `button`, `button_hold` (>= 600 ms) and `button_release`.
- `test "name" { ... }` top level only: skipped by `jlang run` and omitted from native `jlang build`/`emu`, compiled by `jlang check`, and run in isolation with leak checking by `jlang test`.
- `every 500ms { }` repeats, `after 2s { }` runs once; top level only; they start counting when the line runs and run after the top level finishes. `stop_timer()` inside one stops it. Time literals: `500ms` = 500, `2s` = 2000 (ints, ms). Like setInterval/setTimeout; only one handler or timer runs at a time.
- `const NAME = 42` top level only: a compile-time number (int literal, negative literal, another const, or `Enum.MEMBER`), inlined, takes no memory, can't be assigned.
- `enum Mode { BUS, STUDY = 10, ASK }` top level only: scoped zero-RAM compile-time integer constants (`Mode.BUS`, auto-incrementing from 0 or explicit values). Works in exhaustive `match`, `const`, and native code.
- `struct Point { x, y }` top level only (fields on lines or comma separated). `Point { x: 1, y: 2 }` struct, every field required, any order. `p.x`, `p.x = 3`, `p.x += 1`. `free(p)`. Passed by reference; `==` is identity; 8 bytes per field on VM heap; static `.bss` (int fields only, without `free()`) in top-level native RISC-V code.
- Assignment is a statement only: `x = 1`, `x += 1` (also -= *= /= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>=), `buf[i] = v`, `reg[3] = 1`, `reg[7..4] = 5`. Never inside an expression.

## Types
- nil, bool, int (32-bit signed, wraps; no floats), str (read-only bytes), buf (heap bytes), array (list of any values), struct (named fields), ring (fixed-capacity circular FIFO), fn, built-in.
- Literals: `123`, `1_000`, `0xFF`, `0b1010`, `'A'` (=65), `"text\n"` (escapes \n \t \r \0 \\ \" \' \xHH), `true`, `false`, `nil`.
- Truthiness: nil, false, 0 are false; everything else true.

## Operators (low to high precedence)
`||` `&&` (short-circuit, give bool) · `==` `!=` · `<` `<=` `>` `>=` (ints) · `|` · `^` · `&` · `<<` `>>` (0..31, >> arithmetic) · `+` `-` · `*` `/` `%` (truncate toward zero; /0 is an error) · unary `-` `!` `~` · call `f()`, index `x[i]`, bit range `x[hi..lo]`.
NOTE: bitwise binds tighter than comparison: `x & 1 == 0` is `(x & 1) == 0`. `+` with a str on either side joins as text (numbers printed like print) into a NEW HEAP str that must be freed; in a chain "a" + b + c the intermediate strings are freed automatically. `s += x` leaks the old string. `fmt(fmt, ...)` -> heap str with printf placeholders.

## Bits
- `x[i]` on an int reads bit i (0..31) as 0/1. `x[hi..lo]` reads bits hi down to lo.
- On a variable: `x[i] = 0|1|true|false`, `x[hi..lo] = v` (error if v doesn't fit), `x[i] ^= 1`.
- `u8(v)` `i8(v)` `u16(v)` `i16(v)` keep the low bits.

## Memory
- `alloc(n)` returns a zeroed buf of n bytes; every alloc needs exactly one `free(buf)`.
- `compact()` slides live heap blocks together without invalidating any `buf`, `str`, `array`, `struct` or `ring` handle, returning the size in bytes of the single contiguous free block left behind.
- `buf[i]` reads/writes a byte 0..255 (storing outside 0..255 is an error; use u8()).
- `len(x)` for buf/str/array/ring. `read16/read32(buf, off)`, `write16/write32(buf, off, v)` are little-endian.
- Wire-format bit packing: `pack(buf, off, fmt, ...)` packs integer fields into `buf` and returns bytes written; `unpack(buf, off, fmt)` decodes fields into a new array (must `free()`). Format tokens: `u1..u32`, `i1..i32` (MSB-first bitfields), byte-aligned `u16be`/`u16le`/`i16be`/`i16le`/`u24be`/`u24le`/`i24be`/`i24le`/`u32be`/`u32le`/`i32be`/`i32le`, and `padN` (zero padding bits). Out-of-range values fail before mutating `buf`.
- Fixed-capacity ring buffer: `ring(cap)` (heap FIFO, `free(r)` when done), `ring_push(r, v) -> bool`, `ring_pop(r) -> v|nil`, `ring_peek(r) -> v|nil`, `ring_full(r)`, `ring_empty(r)`, `ring_cap(r)`, `ring_clear(r)`, `len(r)` (current count).
- Arrays: `[1, 2, "x"]` (trailing comma ok), `array(n)` (n zeros), `array(n, v)`; `a[i]`, `a[i] = v`, `a[i] += 1`, nested `g[y][x] = 1`; `len(a)` items; `free(a)`; `==` is identity. 8 bytes per item on the VM heap; top-level fixed-size int arrays (and 2D int arrays) live in static `.bss` in native RISC-V code with runtime bounds checks.
- Use after free, double free, out-of-bounds and leaks are detected and reported with line numbers. A leak is a heap block nothing refers to at exit; blocks still referenced by globals are not reported.
- Strings returned by built-ins such as `ask()`, `slice()`, `trim()` and `kv_get()` are on the heap and must be freed. String literals must not be freed.
- `mem()` prints heap stats, `memmap()` prints the block layout.

## Built-ins
stop_timer() · random(lo, hi) inclusive · map(v, a, b, c, d) rescale · clamp(v, lo, hi) · abs(x) · min(a, b) · max(a, b) · sat_add(a, b) · sat_sub(a, b) · fix_mul(a, b, frac) · fix_div(a, b, frac) (frac 0..31, 64-bit intermediate, saturating) · rgb(r, g, b) -> 0xRRGGBB · print(...) · fmt(fmt, ...) -> heap str · printf(fmt, ...) placeholders {} {d} {x} {b} {c} with optional width e.g. {x2} {b8} {d5}, {d05} pads with zeros, `{{ }}` literal braces, no automatic newline · contains(s, sub) -> bool · starts_with(s, pre) -> bool · ends_with(s, suf) -> bool · slice(s, start, end) -> heap str · trim(s) -> heap str · alloc(n) · free(x) (buf, array, struct, ring, heap str) · compact() -> largest free bytes · len(x) · array(n[, v]) · ring(cap) · ring_push(r, v) · ring_pop(r) · ring_peek(r) · ring_full(r) · ring_empty(r) · ring_cap(r) · ring_clear(r) · pack(buf, off, fmt, ...) -> bytes · unpack(buf, off, fmt) -> array · read16 read32 write16 write32 · u8 i8 u16 i16 · mem() · memmap() · cycles() · assert(cond, msg) · emit(name)

## Board built-ins (simulated on desktop, real on device)
pin_mode(pin, "out"|"in"|"in_pullup") · pin_write(pin, 0|1) (pin must be "out") · pin_read(pin) (pin must be an input) · delay(ms) (virtual time) · millis() · capture() -> buf (free it) · record(ms) -> audio buf (sim: --voice TEXT, free it) · record_start() · record_stop() -> audio buf (push-to-talk, free it) · ask(photo_or_nil, prompt_or_audio[, instruction]) -> str (free it) · speak(text, lang="en") · chime("ready"|"working"|"error") · kv_set(key, val) · kv_get(key[, default]) -> heap str or nil (free if non-nil) · kv_del(key) -> bool
Parts (set up the pin themselves, no pin_mode needed): turn_on(pin) · turn_off(pin) · toggle(pin) · brightness(pin, 0..100) PWM · color(pin, "red"|0xRRGGBB) WS2812 LED · color_at(pin, n, colour) strip LED n 0..63 · tone(pin, hz|"C#5"|"rest", ms) blocks for ms · beep(pin) · servo(pin, 0..180) · pressed(pin) -> bool, true once per press of a button to ground, debounced · analog(pin) -> 0..4095 (sim: --analog N=V, default 2048) · distance(trig, echo) -> cm or -1 (sim: --distance CM, default 100). Colour names: red green blue yellow cyan magenta orange purple pink white warm off. These are VM-only: compile errors in native code.

LED panel (sim 60x7, --panel WxH): led(x, y, colour) sets a frame pixel, off-panel ignored · led_clear() · led_show() sends the frame (records millis; browser plays frames at those times) · led_text(text|number, x, y, colour) 5x7 font, 6 px advance, returns next x · led_width() · led_height() · led_size() -> [w, h] array, free it · rgb(r, g, b). led/led_clear/led_show/led_width/led_height/rgb also work in native code.

I2C and SPI: i2c_scan() -> array of addresses (free it) · i2c_write(addr, byte, ...) first byte is usually a register · i2c_read(addr, reg) -> byte · i2c_read16(addr, reg) -> 16-bit, high byte first · spi_write(cs, byte, ...) · spi_transfer(cs, byte) -> byte received. Simulated bus: TMP102 at 0x48 (reg 0: signed 12-bit temperature in 1/16 C in the top bits; C = (i16(i2c_read16(0x48, 0)) >> 4) / 16), MPU-6050 at 0x68 (WHO_AM_I 0x75 = 0x68; starts asleep, i2c_write(0x68, 0x6B, 0) wakes it; accel z 0x3F reads 16384 = 1 g), OLED at 0x3C. Unknown addresses are an error. SPI reads 0xFF in the simulator. VM-only.

## Native code (RISC-V)
- `jlang emu FILE [--emit EVENT] [--asm] [--listing]` compiles to RV32IM and runs on the built-in emulator. `jlang build FILE -o out.s` writes assembly for a real board, which links with a C file implementing boards/jl_hal.h. `jlang asm FILE.s` assembles and runs hand-written assembly.
- Strict native parity contract: a program either behaves identically to the VM or is rejected at compile time with the reason. Native supports ints, bools, nil, string literals and string variables, functions (also as values), loops, exhaustive `match`, `defer`, `enum`, `use ... [as alias]`, top-level static `.bss` int arrays (`[1, 2]`, `array(n[, int_v])`, 2D int arrays, `len(arr)`, runtime bounds checks) and int-field structs (`struct S { ... }`, `s.field`, compile-time field offsets), bits and slices, events, const, print/printf, pins, delay/millis, u8/i8/u16/i16, abs/min/max/clamp/sat_add/sat_sub/fix_mul/fix_div, assert, cycles(), the LED panel. `test` blocks are skipped with zero code size overhead. Functions can only be given numbers and functions and can only return numbers or bools. Arithmetic on bool/nil/str is a compile error; values of different types compare unequal; bool/str/fn variables keep their type. No dynamic heap: `free()`, `alloc()`, `compact()`, `ring()`, `pack()`/`unpack()`, `read16`/`read32`/`write16`/`write32`, non-int arrays/structs, arrays/structs inside functions or loops, printing whole arrays/structs, fmt, string +, string indexing, string helpers, mem/memmap, capture/record/ask/speak/chime, kv_*, timers, part built-ins and I2C/SPI are compile errors.
- The native code generator keeps function locals 1..6 in callee-saved registers (`s2`–`s7`) across loops and calls, keeps expression operands in a 7-register cache (`t3`–`t6`, `a5`–`a7`), folds constants and immediate ALU ops, and fuses comparisons with conditional branches.
- `jlang emu FILE --pipeline [ROWS]` prints a 5-stage pipeline diagram (F D X M W, forwarding, 1-cycle load-use stall, 2 flushed after a taken branch) and CPI for the whole run.
- `mmio_read32(addr)`, `mmio_write32(addr, v)`, `mmio_read8`, `mmio_write8` access hardware registers (also simulated by `jlang run`). Simulated board map: UART 0x10000000 (write a byte), GPIO_DIR 0x10001000, GPIO_PULL 0x10001004, GPIO_OUT 0x10001008, GPIO_IN 0x1000100C, TIMER_MS 0x10002000, TIMER_WAIT 0x10002004.
- `asm("li t0, 1; addi t0, t0, 2")` inserts RISC-V instructions (native only; `;` separates instructions; the string must be a literal). Registers s0, s1 and sp belong to JLang and must be restored.
- Native runtime errors print `runtime error (line L): message` and stop the program.

## Example
```
let LED = 2
pin_mode(LED, "out")
let status = 0
status[7..4] = 0b1010
on button {
    let photo = capture()
    let answer = ask(photo, "What bus is this?")
    free(photo)
    speak(answer, "en")
    free(answer)
    pin_write(LED, 1)
}
```
